Finding.Text: Evidence recorded by the 0.3.0 kernel does not survive the 0.3.0 to 0.4.0 upgrade, and the revision-1 documents said it does. The candidate rule changed with this change, not only the pin: 0.3.0 hashed the pin into the candidate and 0.4.0 leaves it out, so every revision that carries a pin has a different candidate under the two kernels; a start run recorded by the v0.3.0 checkout read "does not count: recorded on an earlier candidate, recorded with grace5 0.3.0" under 0.4.0 and close refused, while upgrade.md said "invalidates no evidence" and the source-identity.md example row said "The result still counts". The pilot named in Problem will find every result and every review stale once; the close records written with the pin included (C-0004's 8907d111) no longer reproduce under this kernel.
Finding.Resolution: Resolved in revision 2 by stating the boundary where the rule is amended, and the statements match the kernel. source-identity.md gained a paragraph after the rule: the exclusion dates from 0.4.0, a pinned tree has one candidate under 0.3.0 and another under 0.4.0, results and reviews recorded by 0.3.0 on a pinned tree do not count under 0.4.0 and are rerun and re-reviewed, an unpinned tree is unaffected, and a closed record is read by the rule of the kernel it names; the example row now says "None for a result recorded under this rule" and that a 0.3.0 result on a pinned tree is on an earlier candidate "whether or not the pin is written". upgrade.md's pin section drops "invalidates no evidence", states the same boundary with the exact status line, says an unpinned tree has the same candidate under both rules, and that a close.xml written by 0.3.0 reproduces with the pin included; the ways-out paragraph adds that across this boundary the 0.3.0 results and review are redone first. The contract's Change carries the same sentence, so the owner approved the cost on brief-2. Verified by probe: a receipt written by the real v0.3.0 kernel on a pinned tree reads exactly as the document says before and after this kernel's upgrade and counts again after a rerun; a v0.2.0 clone has candidate d95fd1f1 under both kernels; the close candidate of C-0004 reproduces by hand with the pin included (8907d111) and not without (e4604ae4). UP-18 pins the stale-under-0.4.0 reading with a receipt rewritten to the 0.3.0 rule's candidate (the helper's computeCandidate with pinIncluded) and the counting of a result this kernel records across a pin rewrite, removal, upgrade and commit; the case uses an edited receipt rather than a 0.3.0 kernel, which the reviewer's probe supplies. The skills and README do not repeat the boundary; upgrade.md, which both skills cite for the upgrade, carries it, and the contract did not ask for more.

Finding.Text: Revision 1 altered two skills and shipped no migration step, against method.md line 79 and upgrade.md ("A kernel change that alters the state layout, the ignore lines or the skills ships its step in the same change"); the 0.3.0 to 0.4.0 boundary was a pin bump, skills are refreshed on a step only, and a pilot at 0.3.0 with the grace5-* directories installed kept the 0.3.0 skill text after upgrading, with no kernel facility to refresh it.
Finding.Resolution: Resolved in revision 2 by the step refreshTheSkills (0.3.0 to 0.4.0, "refresh the installed skills to 0.4.0"): apply does nothing, the runner's refresh does the work, verify fails with the differing paths when any installed grace5-* skill file differs from the packaged one, touches is empty, writes is the installed skill files that differ; STEPS is three steps and the contract's Change now says so. The runner's order became apply, refresh, verify, so a step may count the installed skills as part of its shape; for the two earlier steps the reorder is harmless, since their verify reads the moved directories, the ignore line and the pin and not the skills, and refreshSkills throws before verify only when the packaged skills are missing, which already failed the chain before. The cost of the reorder is that a step whose verify fails has already refreshed the skills, where before it had not; the refresh is idempotent and the next upgrade repeats it, and the pin is still not written, so the repository stays at a consistent version. upgrade.md's step table carries the new row, the sentence that a skills change ships its step is now true of this change, commands.md and the help describe the apply, refresh, verify order and the plan line. Verified by probe on a HEAD clone pinned 0.3.0 with the v0.3.0 skills installed: with C-0005 open the upgrade refuses naming both stale files and proceeds with --accept-evidence-loss, refreshing all three installed directories to byte-equality with the packaged 0.4.0 copies and pinning 0.4.0; with no open change it refreshes without the flag; with no skills installed it prints "skills: none installed" and pins. UP-03 asserts the step line, UP-07 three steps and six refreshed lines, UP-05 the step applied twice, UP-13 three steps with no touches, and the verifier three steps and no bump; notes.md records that each of these fails on the revision-1 tree. The step's verify failure path cannot be reached from the CLI after a successful refresh and is not exercised by a test; see F5.

Finding.Text: In revision 1 "evidence of open changes becomes history: <id>" was printed whenever --accept-evidence-loss was given with changes open, including when the union of writes was empty and nothing became history.
Finding.Resolution: Resolved in revision 2: the line requires open.length > 0, writes.length > 0 and the flag; commands.md ("and at least one writes: line"), upgrade.md ("with nothing to write the flag changes nothing and the line is not printed"), the help text and UP-14 say so, the contract's Change carries "The evidence line is printed only when a source write was pending", and UP-12 asserts the flag with nothing to write prints neither writes nor the evidence line and leaves the candidate. Verified by probe: a HEAD clone without a pin, C-0005 open and no skills, upgrade --accept-evidence-loss prints the three steps and "open, untouched" and no evidence line, writes only the pin, and every result still counts; the same clone with a stale skill prints the line once, before the first refreshed line.

Finding.Text: The start run's CK6 result reads verdict="passed" on the 0.3.0 kernel because the 0.3.0 verifier ignored arguments it did not know and ran the plain check; that pass is not evidence of what the check claims.
Finding.Resolution: Nothing in the tree could change: a receipt is never rewritten (K2) and the start result is not counted at close. notes.md now records the spurious pass and why, and the verifier has refused unknown arguments since revision 1 (probed: exit 1 on --bogus). Carried as resolved on that record; a reader of run-1.xml is pointed to notes.md.

Finding.Text: refreshTheSkills.verify compares the installed skills with the kernel's default packaged directory (skillWrites(root), no second argument), while the refresh that precedes it and the step's own writes use the packaged directory the runner was given (input.packagedSkills). The Step interface gives verify no way to receive it. Today nothing injects one: no test or command passes packagedSkills to applyUpgrade, so refresh and verify compare against the same files and the probes and UP-07 pass. The first test or tool that injects another packaged directory to drive the refresh will refresh from one set and verify against another, and the 0.3.0 to 0.4.0 step will fail or pass for the wrong reason. The verify failure path is otherwise unreachable after a successful mirror and no test exercises it, so this inconsistency has no test to catch it. Either thread the packaged directory through verify as writes already has it, or state in the Step interface that verify compares against the kernel's own packaged skills.
